sub_graphs.title: Fulu Polynomial Commitments: Cell Proof Generation
sub_graphs.description: Models the process of generating KZG proofs for individual cells from blob data using polynomial commitment schemes

nodes.label: Raw Blob Data Received
nodes.description: A blob of FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB field elements has been received for commitment

nodes.label: Reed-Solomon Extend Blob
nodes.description: Extend the blob to FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB (double length) using Reed-Solomon encoding for erasure coding

nodes.label: Extended Blob Ready
nodes.description: Blob has been extended to double length with redundancy for erasure recovery

nodes.label: Partition into Cells
nodes.description: Divide extended blob into CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB cells, each containing 64 field elements

nodes.label: Compute KZG Proof for Each Cell
nodes.description: For each cell, compute quotient polynomial Q(X) = f(X)/Z(X) where Z(X) vanishes on evaluation points, yielding a KZG proof

nodes.label: Cells and KZG Proofs Generated
nodes.description: All cells have associated KZG proofs ready for distribution

external_entities.name: Block Producer
external_entities.description: The validator proposing a block that includes blob data requiring commitment proofs

sub_graphs.title: Fulu Polynomial Commitments: Batch Cell Verification
sub_graphs.description: Models the batch verification of multiple cell KZG proofs using Fiat-Shamir challenge aggregation

nodes.label: Cells and Proofs Received for Verification
nodes.description: Multiple (commitment, cell, proof) tuples have been received and need verification

nodes.label: Deduplicate Commitments
nodes.description: Identify unique commitments to optimize verification by avoiding redundant pairing computations

nodes.label: Derive Fiat-Shamir Challenge
nodes.description: Hash all commitments, cell indices, cells, and proofs to derive random challenge r for aggregation

nodes.label: Aggregate with r-Powers
nodes.description: Combine all commitment-proof pairs using powers of r to create a single aggregated verification equation

nodes.label: Execute Pairing Check
nodes.description: Verify the universal equation: pairing(LL, LR) == pairing(RL, [1]) using BLS12-381 pairings

nodes.label: Batch Verification Passed
nodes.description: All cell proofs are valid with overwhelming probability

nodes.label: Batch Verification Failed
nodes.description: At least one cell proof is invalid; individual verification needed to identify which

external_entities.name: Data Column Provider
external_entities.description: Node providing DataColumnSidecars containing cells and KZG proofs for verification

sub_graphs.title: Fulu Polynomial Commitments: Cell Recovery via Polynomial Interpolation
sub_graphs.description: Models the recovery of missing cells from partial data using FFT-based polynomial reconstruction

nodes.label: Partial Cell Set Available
nodes.description: At least 50% of cells for a blob are available, enabling polynomial recovery

nodes.label: Construct Vanishing Polynomial
nodes.description: Build polynomial Z(X) that vanishes on the evaluation domains of missing cells

nodes.label: Multiply by Zero Polynomial in Eval Form
nodes.description: Multiply available cell evaluations by the zero polynomial to prepare for division

nodes.label: Perform Coset FFT Division
nodes.description: Use coset-shifted FFT to divide out the vanishing polynomial, recovering the original polynomial coefficients

nodes.label: Evaluate Recovered Polynomial
nodes.description: Evaluate the recovered polynomial at all cell domains to regenerate missing cells

nodes.label: Recompute KZG Proofs for Recovered Cells
nodes.description: Generate fresh KZG proofs for the reconstructed cells

nodes.label: All Cells and Proofs Recovered
nodes.description: Complete cell set with valid KZG proofs has been reconstructed

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions O(n^2) complexity for compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs and recommends FK20 for production, but does not mandate a specific algorithm.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations may use either the naive O(n^2) or FK20 algorithm, as the specification treats this as an optimization choice. Security analysis should consider the naive algorithm as the baseline.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs receives exactly the minimum number of cells (50%) but some are corrupted is not specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume corrupted cells are detected via KZG proof verification before recovery, so only verified cells are counted toward the 50% threshold.

implicit_assumptions.description: The BLS12-381 trusted setup ceremony was performed correctly, and the toxic waste was destroyed.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: An entity with the toxic waste could forge KZG proofs, creating valid-looking commitments for arbitrary data and breaking data availability guarantees.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot solve the discrete logarithm problem on BLS12-381 in practical time.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Complete break of the polynomial commitment scheme, enabling forged proofs and fake data availability.

implicit_assumptions.description: Nodes have sufficient computational resources to perform FFT-based polynomial recovery and pairing checks within slot time.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Nodes unable to verify proofs in time may accept invalid data or miss attestation deadlines.
